title: Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program Liability Notices and Patient Charge Types
content:
When an item or quantity the customer wants is expected not to be paid by the payer — above the tier's allowance without supporting documentation, an item the tier does not cover, or a replacement before the payer's replacement interval — Larkfield supplies it on the Insulin and Injection Supply Pharmacy Program billable to the customer only after the customer signs the tier's liability notice for that item and quantity before the ship date; the customer signs it personally, and no Larkfield representative can sign it for them.

## The notice by tier

- **Original Medicare tier.** The notice is the CMS Advance Beneficiary Notice of Noncoverage (form CMS-R-131); the claim is still submitted to Medicare with the notice on file, and the customer becomes liable only for a line Medicare denies.
- **Medicare Advantage tier.** No notice can make the member liable; the member becomes liable only for an item for which the plan has issued a pre-service organization determination denial, recorded as a prior authorization denial for that item.
- **Self-pay tier.** No notice applies, because every item is priced at the Larkfield cash price.
- **Other tiers.** The notice is the form listed for the tier among the liability notice forms (plan member waiver; Medicaid non-covered service agreement; organization determination required).

## Patient charge types

A patient charge is posted only as one of these charge types:

1. **Self-pay price** — a self-pay refill at the cash price;
2. **Standard shipping** — a self-pay shipment below the free-shipping threshold, at the tier's standard shipping fee;
3. **Expedited shipping** — a customer-requested expedite, at the tier's expedited shipping fee;
4. **Non-covered item** — an item or quantity covered by a signed liability notice, or by a Medicare Advantage organization determination denial, that the payer denied, charged at the Larkfield cash price of the units concerned.

## Condition for a non-covered item charge

A non-covered item charge requires a liability notice signed on or before the ship date covering that item and at least those units, or on the Medicare Advantage tier the plan's organization determination denial for that item; without it the amount is Larkfield's write-off and is never billed to the customer. The signed notice, or the denial, is read from the program's records for that item.

| Hypothetical case (payer denied 4 units of an item) | Charge to the customer? |
|---|---|
| Notice signed two days before the ship date, covering that item and 4 units | Yes — non-covered item at the cash price of the 4 units |
| Notice signed on the ship date, covering that item and 6 units | Yes — signed on or before the ship date, covering at least those units |
| Notice signed covering that item but only 2 units | No — the notice does not cover at least those units; Larkfield's write-off |
| Notice signed the day after the ship date | No — Larkfield's write-off |
| Medicare Advantage tier; the plan's organization determination denial for that item on file | Yes — non-covered item at the cash price of the units concerned |
